nodes.statement: A glimmer on a curve $X$ is a pair $(F,s)$ with $s$ a section of $F$ vanishing at exactly $\deg F$ points.
If $(F,s)$ is a glimmer, $F(1)$ has a section $s'$ agreeing with $s$ off the zeros of $s$.
Every glimmer $(F,s)$ of degree $d\ge1$ splits after one twist: $F(1)$ is a sum of line bundles.
nodes.intuition: [Claude] The twist makes the section extend, so the sheaf is generated off finitely many points and Grothendieck's theorem applies.

A1.ref: R. Ash: Fictional sheaves I. J. Fict. Geom. 1 (2029).

G.ref: A. Grothendieck: Sur la classification des fibrés holomorphes sur la sphère de Riemann (1957).
